name: chgrp
description: Changes the group ownership of files and directories.

flags.description: Copy the group from another file.

examples.explanation: Changes the group of report.txt to developers (you must be a member of that group, or use sudo).
Recursively assigns uploaded files to the web server group so it can read them.

examples.output: changed group of 'README.md' from user to team
examples.explanation: Verbose mode reports each file whose group changed.

about: chgrp changes only the group, keeping the owner untouched — it is exactly chown :GROUP. A regular user may change the group of their own files to any group they belong to; changing to arbitrary groups requires root.
useCases: Hand files to a team or service group.
Fix group ownership of web content.
mistakes: Trying to chgrp to a group you are not a member of without sudo.
